chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Tirbal said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who divorced his wife with a single divorce before consummating the marriage, and he testified to that and informed her. He said: She becomes permanently divorced from him at the moment he divorces her, while she is still considered among the suitors (not yet in a new waiting period). I said: If he marries her again and then divorces her with another single divorce before consummating the marriage? He said: She becomes permanently divorced from him at the moment he divorces her. I said: If he marries her again immediately and then divorces her with a single divorce? He said: She becomes permanently divorced from him, and she is not permissible to him until she marries another husband.

key_terms.بَانَتْ مِنْهُ: She became permanently divorced/separated from him
key_terms.خَاطِبٌ مِنَ الْخُطَّابِ: Considered among the suitors (status of the wife before consummation)
key_terms.قَبْلَ أَنْ يَدْخُلَ بِهَا: Before consummation (entering the room with the wife)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a man divorces his wife before consummating the marriage in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: In al-Istibsar, Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifying that a divorce issued before consummation (dakhil) results in an immediate, irrevocable separation (banan), distinct from the standard revocable divorce. This highlights the Shia juristic view that the marital bond is fully severed upon the utterance of the divorce formula in this context, requiring a new contract (aqd) for remarriage. The final clause reinforces the 'three divorces' principle, where she remains forbidden to him until she marries another man and is subsequently divorced or widowed.
